title: spec(security): the `postureStampsOrganization` docblock says the enterprise runtime stamps `organization_id` and the open engine only validates, the opposite of the code and of its own file header
body:
domain:devx#2 · marchtian · session_017ihL2gLghEqeDKTbDTC7Zd

Filing gate: ① a defect with a named location: a published `@objectstack/spec` docblock states the opposite of what the code does. Found while landing #28703, the same defect in `packages/verify/src/harness.ts`.
Reader: `domain:spec`, one docblock patch in `packages/spec/src/security/tenancy-posture.ts` (comment only; it ships in `dist/security/index.d.ts`, so a patch changeset).
Dedupe (open AND closed): "postureStampsOrganization" → #28703 (the verify half, which leaves spec alone), #12699, #10031, #18378, #14291 (none about this docblock).
reach: measured from source at `origin/main` 2026-11-01 (#28703 PR head `5b630f038e`).
type: Bug

Business reason: `postureStampsOrganization` is the shared vocabulary for the write half of the tenant wall. A reader who trusts its docblock believes stamping needs the enterprise runtime, which is how #28703's stale verify docblock came about: test authors skipped cheap cross-tenant pins as "vacuous".

## Where

`packages/spec/src/security/tenancy-posture.ts`, the docblock above `export function postureStampsOrganization` (around lines 57–68): "The STAMPER, however, is the enterprise `@objectstack/organizations` runtime, not the open engine … the open engine only VALIDATES supplied values".

## What the code does

- The same file's header (around line 26) already says "the D5 write stamping all ship in open packages".
- The open engine lands an insert in the caller's active organization (`ObjectQL#driverWriteTarget`, `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts`), and the SQL driver fills an absent `organization_id` from it (`SqlDriver#injectTenantOnInsert`, `packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts`).
- What needs the enterprise runtime is ACTIVATING a walled posture (ADR-0105 D12), not the stamping.

## Done when

The docblock says the open engine stamps under a walled posture and names where, and keeps the true half (activation needs the enterprise runtime). No code change. A spec change, so the review rule for spec PRs applies.

⛔ Not a claim.
